questions.stem: Why is methane measured in CO2 equivalent (CO2e) when calculating carbon footprints?

options.text: Because methane and carbon dioxide are always released together
Because methane is actually a form of carbon dioxide
Because different greenhouse gases have different warming potentials, so they are converted to a common unit for comparison
Because methane is too difficult to measure directly

questions.explanation: Different greenhouse gases trap different amounts of heat. Methane is about 25 times more potent than CO2 as a greenhouse gas, and nitrous oxide is about 300 times more potent. Converting all gases to CO2 equivalent allows meaningful comparison and a single total figure for carbon footprint.
